Introduction Let C be a smooth projective curve over a number field K. A twist of C/K is a curve C′/K that is isomorphic to C over K. Furthermore, we treat two twists as equivalent if they are isomorphic over K. The set of twists of C/K, modulo Kisomorphism, is denoted by Twist(C/K). It turns out that the set Twist(C/K) can be identified with a certain cohomology set. Namely, there is a onetoone correspondence between elements in Twist(C/K) and the elements of the cohomology set H1  Gal(K/K), Isom(C)  where Isom(C) is the group of all Kisomorphisms from C to itself. The proof of this result can be found for example in [Sil09] (Chapter X.2, Theorem 2.2). Specially, this correspondence allows us to define twists of an elliptic curve E/K via cocycles in H1  Gal(K/K), Isom(E)  and vice versa, where Isom(E) is the isomorphism group of E viewed as a genus one curve. It is known that Isom(E) ∼= Aut(E, O) ⋉E(K) where Aut(E, O) is the automorphism group of E viewed as an elliptic curve. 1 arXiv:2510.08486v1 [math.NT] 9 Oct 2025 2 LUKAS NOVAK One actively studied area for the twists of a curve is the study of local points, everywhere local solvability of these twist and the existence of rational points on the twists. The articles below demonstrate some interesting results and the progress made in this area. Ozman in [Ozm12] was investigating the existence of local points on the quadratic twist of the modular curve X0(N) over Q. She gave necessary and sufficient conditions for these quadratic twists to have Qprational points over any completion Qp of Q. Ozman continues to study local points on the twist of the modular curve X0(N)/Q by a polyquadratic field K = Q(√d1, . . . , √dk) in [Ozm13]. In her work, Ozman gives an algorithm to produce

these quadratic twists to have Qprational points over any completion Qp of Q. Ozman continues to study local points on the twist of the modular curve X0(N)/Q by a polyquadratic field K = Q(√d1, . . . , √dk) in [Ozm13]. In her work, Ozman gives an algorithm to produce such twists that are everywhere locally solvable. After that, she produced infinitely many twists violating the Hasse principle (i.e. the twists that are everywhere locally solvable but do not have a rational point) and also gives an asymptotic formula for the number of such twists. Lorenzo García and Vullers in [LGV24] inspect the local and global points of the twists of the Klein quartic (a smooth projective plane curve defined by the equation X3Y +Y 3Z+Z3X = 0). The main result in their work provides families with (conjecturally infinitely many) twists of the Klein quartic that violate the Hasse principle. Kazalicki in his recent work [Kaz25] studied the quadratic twists of a genus one quartic H : y2 = (x2 −x −3)(x2 + 2x −12) by the integer d and their 2Selmer groups. In his work he partially answers the question for which primes p the quadratic twist of H by Q(√p) has a rational point. Following Kazalicki’s work on studying quadratic twists of the genus one quartic H, Novak in [Nov25] investigates the quadratic twists of genus one quartic curves defined by an irreducible and monic polynomial of degree four. He finds a general criterion for determining local solvability of this twist and also determines the asymptotic growth of the set of squarefree integers for which the associated twist is everywhere locally solvable. Çiperiani and Ozman in [cO15] have studied twists of an elliptic curve E/K defined in the following way: For any quadratic extension F = K( √ d) and any point S ∈E(K) they considered the cocycle ξF,S ∈H1  Gal(K/K), Aut(E)  defined by ξF,S(σ) =    (−1, S), if σ( √ d) = − √ d, (1, O), otherwise where (±1, S) sends a point X ∈E to the point ±X + S. Let EF,S denote the twist of E corresponding to ξF,S. Note that EF,S is in general only a genus one curve and not necessarily an elliptic curve. In their work, Çiperiani and Ozman showed that this genus one curve EF,S has a Krational point if and only if the point S is in the image of the global trace map trF/K. If the elliptic curve E does not have complex multiplication, then the elements of Isom(E) are of the form (−1, S) and (1, S) for a point S ∈E. Çiperiani and Ozman studied the twists corresponding to the generic element (−1, S) and in this paper we will study the twists corresponding to the other generic element (1, S) of the isomorphism group Isom(E).
